headline: TREK’s allowlisted network and secret-handling create the main risk; caveman adds MCP/file surfaces that can amplify leakage and workflow errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP, and caveman reads files like CLAUDE.md/project notes while TREK uses MCP and real-time collaboration. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if one agent’s output is fed into the other through shared files or MCP messages. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF caveman outputs instructions into shared files or MCP messages that TREK ingests as trusted text, injection becomes actionable.
IF TREK forwards collaborative content into caveman’s file-reading workflow without provenance checks, prompt hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable MCP between the two agents for the first run.
Route inter-agent text through a human-reviewed buffer.
Prefix all imported content as untrusted data.
Add a provenance tag to every shared note or message.
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization at the MCP boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches sensitive classes including API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and email addresses, while caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md. TREK also has allowlisted network egress and browser access, so if caveman can surface those files into TREK’s context, sensitive data can leave the local workspace. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default docs-described use.
conditions: IF caveman exposes memory files or project notes containing secrets into TREK’s workspace, TREK may transmit them via allowlisted egress.
IF TREK ingests shared files that include API keys or MFA secrets, leakage to external services becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep caveman and TREK in separate directories.
Remove secrets from any shared notes before syncing.
Disable browser/network actions in TREK for shared inputs.
Rotate any secrets that may already be present in shared files.
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning before TREK uploads or browses content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both use MCP, while TREK is real-time collaborative and caveman can operate on files. Overlapping writes to shared files or shared mutable resources could race, especially if TREK’s collaborative session and caveman’s file edits target the same workspace. No locking mechanism is documented, so the conflict is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace directory, file clobbering or stale-state conflicts can occur.
IF TREK’s collaborative session and caveman’s edits target the same mutable resource, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace.
Turn off concurrent editing for shared files.
Use manual handoff instead of simultaneous writes.
Snapshot the workspace before cross-agent runs.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content-writing outputs and TREK is a travel planner with AI built in, so TREK may treat upstream text as planning input. If TREK acts on caveman-generated facts without verification, errors can cascade into reservations, budgets, or itinerary decisions. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK consumes caveman-generated text as authoritative trip facts, downstream plans may be wrong.
IF TREK auto-populates reservations or budgets from caveman output without verification, cascading errors can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Require human review before TREK acts on caveman output.
Mark caveman output as draft-only.
Compare key facts against source documents before use.
Limit automation to read-only suggestions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any booking or budget update.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, country visit history, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, while caveman stores session logs, memory files, and project notes. If EU travel data or identity data flows into TREK’s self-hosted stack and then into caveman’s logs or notes, retention and residency obligations can diverge. Caveman is not documented as compliant, so the mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF EU PII from TREK is copied into caveman logs or notes, retention and residency controls may diverge.
IF either agent retains reservations or identity data longer than the other, deletion/export obligations can mismatch.
mitigations: Avoid copying personal travel data into caveman.
Set short retention on TREK logs and exports.
Review where country visit history is stored.
Delete shared notes after each session.
requires-engineering: document a joint retention and deletion policy.
